description:
REQ-124's cross-loan tx_hash-replay guard (impl-review iteration-3, resolves FIND-201) and its own iteration-2 antecedent (verifyRepayment's alreadyCredited check, REQ-108e/FIND-202) both compare tx_hash values with raw, case-sensitive strict equality (`row.tx_hash === txHash`) at lending-verify.mjs:85 and lending-verify.mjs:175. Neither side of either comparison is normalized. This codebase already demonstrates explicit awareness that hex-string identity must be compared case-insensitively when the two sides can originate from different sources/serializers: lending-signer.mjs:32-34's addressesEqual() exists FOR EXACTLY THIS REASON ('checksummed vs. lowercased forms of the SAME address must compare equal') and is used for every wallet-address comparison in this feature (REQ-119). tx_hash values are the SAME class of hex string (32-byte keccak output) but receive NO equivalent normalization anywhere in lending-verify.mjs or lending-orchestrator.mjs.

This is not a theoretical nit: tx_hash values in loans.jsonl are populated from TWO STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT sources with no shared, code-enforced casing contract: (1) the happy-path disbursement route -- lending-orchestrator.mjs:423 stores `disburseResult.tx`, which is `settle.json.transaction` (escrow.mjs:133,139), a raw field parsed out of an HTTP JSON response from the SELF-HOSTED FACILITATOR -- an external, third-party Rust codebase (x402-rs, wired as a git submodule at services/facilitator/x402-rs per .gitmodules, NOT present/reviewable in this repo checkout and NOT written or controlled by this feature); vs. (2) the reconciliation route -- lending-verify.mjs:174/179's extractTxHash(log) reads `log.transactionHash` directly off THIS codebase's own `eth_getLogs` call against https://mainnet.base.org. Nothing in this diff, this feature's spec, or its tests asserts, tests, or even documents that x402-rs's own `/settle` response `transaction` field and Base mainnet's own `eth_getLogs` `transactionHash` field are guaranteed to serialize the SAME real transaction hash with IDENTICAL character casing.

This is precisely the collision path REQ-124 exists to close: loan A disburses successfully via the happy path (tx_hash stored in facilitator-format, lending-orchestrator.mjs:423), loan B (the SAME lender/borrower pair's very next cold-start attempt -- REQ-124's own stated hazard scenario, computeLoanCapUsd's flat $0.02 cap) gets stuck and its resolveStaleProvisioning reconcile scan (eth_getLogs, same wallet pair, same window) finds loan A's OWN already-settled transfer (same value, same pair, well within the ~5h lookback). If x402-rs's `/settle` response ever returns the transaction hash in a DIFFERENT case than mainnet.base.org's eth_getLogs `transactionHash` field for that SAME transaction (e.g. mixed-case vs. lowercase -- there is no EIP-55-style canonical checksum convention for TRANSACTION hashes the way there is for addresses, so no cross-implementation guarantee exists), the `alreadyRecorded` check at lending-verify.mjs:175 silently fails to match, loan B is falsely marked `active` on loan A's own real transfer, and loan A's own row (which never got a second chance at reconciliation, since it is now already `active`) permanently misrepresents that money was received twice -- the EXACT active fund-misattribution hazard iteration-3's own FIND-201 was written to close, reopened by an unnormalized string comparison.

None of the new FIND-201 tests can catch this: every fixture in both lending-verify.test.mjs (lines 301-348) and lending-orchestrator.test.mjs (lines 375-407) uses the IDENTICAL literal string for both the 'already recorded' loanRows.tx_hash value and the freshly-extracted candidate's transactionHash -- the fixtures assume same-source, same-casing values throughout, which is true for every OTHER already-tested code path (both extracted via extractTxHash from the SAME mock RPC) but is NOT true for the realistic happy-path-disbursement-then-later-reconciled-by-a-different-row scenario this finding describes.
recommendation: Normalize BOTH sides of every tx_hash comparison to lowercase before storing (activeStatusFields/appendLoanRow call sites in lending-orchestrator.mjs) and before comparing (verifyRepayment's alreadyCredited, reconcileProvisionalDisbursement's alreadyRecorded, and executeRepaymentClaim's own txHash usage) -- mirror lending-signer.mjs's own addressesEqual() precedent exactly (`String(a).toLowerCase() === String(b).toLowerCase()`), or introduce an equivalent `txHashesEqual` helper reused at every comparison site. Add a test fixture that stores an 'already recorded' tx_hash in one case and supplies the SAME logical hash in a DIFFERENT case as the freshly-extracted candidate, asserting the guard still rejects it -- this is the only way to prove REQ-124/REQ-108e's stated guarantee actually holds across the facilitator-format vs. RPC-format source boundary, not merely within a single mock RPC's own self-consistent casing.
